deck.name: Clouds & Weather
deck.description: Cloud types, instruments, storms and how the atmosphere works.

questions.prompt: Which clouds are high, thin and wispy, made of ice crystals?
Which cloud type produces thunderstorms?
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds can also produce hail and tornadoes.

questions.prompt: Which clouds form a low, flat, grey layer that often covers the whole sky?
In cloud names, what does "nimbus" or "nimbo-" indicate?
Which prefix marks mid-level clouds, such as altocumulus?
Fog is a cloud that forms at ground level.
Which instrument measures air pressure?
Which instrument measures wind speed?
Which instrument measures humidity?
What is the dew point?
questions.answer: The temperature to which air must cool to become saturated, so water vapour starts to condense.

questions.prompt: Which scale rates tornado strength in the United States?
Which scale categorises hurricanes by wind speed?
questions.explanation: It runs from Category 1 to Category 5.

questions.prompt: Hurricanes in the Northern Hemisphere spin counterclockwise.
questions.explanation: In the Southern Hemisphere they spin clockwise, because of the Coriolis effect.

questions.prompt: In which layer of the atmosphere does almost all weather happen?
What causes thunder?
choices: Air expanding rapidly after being heated by lightning

questions.prompt: What is it called when a cold air mass pushes under and replaces warmer air?
Who proposed the cloud-naming system (cirrus, cumulus, stratus, nimbus) in 1802–1803?
When you see a rainbow, the sun is behind you.
What causes the Coriolis effect, which deflects winds?
choices: The tilt of the Earth's axis

questions.prompt: El Niño refers to unusually warm surface water in which ocean region?
choices: The central and eastern tropical Pacific

questions.prompt: Hurricane, typhoon and tropical cyclone are names for the same kind of storm. What decides which name is used?
choices: Where in the world it forms
questions.explanation: Hurricanes form in the Atlantic and northeast Pacific, typhoons in the northwest Pacific, and cyclones in the South Pacific and Indian Ocean.

questions.prompt: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.explanation: Tall structures are hit repeatedly. The Empire State Building is struck about 20 to 25 times a year.

questions.prompt: Which unit is common for air pressure on weather maps?
questions.explanation: One hectopascal equals one millibar. Both names are common in weather reports.

questions.prompt: What is a lenticular cloud?
questions.answer: A smooth, lens-shaped cloud that forms over mountains when moist air flows over them.

questions.prompt: What are the white trails that aircraft leave across the sky?
questions.explanation: Contrails are condensation trails. Water in aircraft exhaust forms ice crystals in cold upper air.

questions.prompt: What scale measures wind force from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force)?
